title: The Pale Gravity
premise: Jude Okonkwo, a xenolinguist stationed on the dying colony of Meridian-9, has spent years translating the songs of the native tide-creatures while the colonial administration quietly abandons the outpost. When gravity across the entire system stutters for nine seconds, Jude realizes the creatures' latest song cycle is not a mating call but a countdown — and that the alien intelligence beneath the ice has been broadcasting a peace offer the warring human fleets have been misreading as a threat. Racing against an expiring truce, Jude must smuggle the true translation to both fleet commands through a smuggler crew she's come to love as family, knowing the message will expose her own government's role in starting the war. In the end, she broadcasts it herself from the collapsing colony, sacrificing her anonymity and nearly her life; the truth ends the war, the colony is evacuated rather than erased, and Jude finally dreams in two languages at once.
about_author: Orsen Amberdale is the pen name of a former deep-sea acoustics technician who spent six years recording whale song off the Hebrides before turning to fiction. They write slow-burning science fiction about people who listen when everyone else has stopped.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. During a routine recording session in the ice tunnels, gravity flickers system-wide for exactly nine seconds, killing three colonists and shattering Jude's equipment. Amid the panic, she notices the tide-creatures' song changed pitch mid-flicker. Emotional beat: quiet dread — the universe just cleared its throat.

chapters.title: The Colony That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Establishing life on Meridian-9: dwindling supplies, an administrator who files false reports to hide the abandonment, and Jude's found family — engineer Sefa, medic twins Idris and Noor, and smuggler captain Rhee Voss. Emotional beat: tender melancholy; they are all pretending this home isn't dying.

chapters.title: Songs Without Sleepers
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Jude admits privately that she no longer dreams in English or Yoruba — only in the creatures' tonal grammar. She replays pre-flicker recordings and finds a repeating nine-note motif embedded in months of song. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: POV: Rhee Voss. The smuggler captain receives a fleet-wide bulletin: the ceasefire between Earth's Concord and the Breakaway Compact expires in forty days. Her route past Meridian-9 will be a firing line afterward. Emotional beat: pragmatic fear; war is a schedule now.

chapters.title: What the Ice Was Saying
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Decoding with Sefa's help, Jude maps the nine-note motif to timestamps — it predicted the gravity flicker to the second. The creatures aren't singing about the flicker; they caused it. Or announced it. Emotional beat: vertigo of realization.

chapters.title: The Archive Nobody Reads
chapters.summary: POV: Idris. Digging through colonial records, Idris finds that the first survey team classified the creatures as non-sentient based on a translation error — one Jude's own mentor signed off on. Emotional beat: betrayal; the war's first casualty was accuracy.

chapters.title: Rhee's Price
chapters.summary: POV: Rhee Voss. Jude asks Rhee to carry a message packet to the nearest relay. Rhee refuses: transmitting unverified alien contact data would make them all traitors to both fleets. But she doesn't say no forever. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Second Flicker
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Gravity stutters again — four seconds this time — and the pattern is unmistakable: decreasing intervals, like a countdown. A tremor breaches the ice shelf above the settlement. Emotional beat: terror made mathematical.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Tide
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. In a fever after exposure during the breach rescue, Jude dreams fully in the creatures' language and wakes understanding the song's structure: it is not a threat display. It is a diplomatic address, repeated for years, unanswered. Emotional beat: grief and awe entwined.

chapters.title: The Message Beneath the Message
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Full translation attempt reveals the core: the creatures offer shared terraforming of Meridian-9's oceans — and evidence that the Concord's first strike on the Compact was ordered to silence their own xenolinguists who'd heard the address. Emotional beat: the truth is heavier than any weapon.

chapters.title: Family Vote
chapters.summary: POV: Sefa. The five colonists argue over what to do: stay silent, flee, or broadcast. Sefa forces the vote that binds them — they will send it together, making themselves complicit in each other's fates. Emotional beat: found family choosing risk over safety.

chapters.title: Relay Station Kestrel
chapters.summary: POV: Rhee Voss. Rhee flies the packet toward the relay, dodging Concord pickets, and discovers the station garrison is executing orders to jam all civilian traffic before the truce expires. Emotional beat: the machinery of war grinding smaller and smaller escapes.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Ghost
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. A Concord patrol boards Meridian-9, hunting 'unregistered signals.' An officer recognizes Jude's name from the suppressed linguistics files. She talks her way through the interrogation by telling the truth so precisely it sounds like nonsense. Emotional beat: invisibility failing, nerve holding.

chapters.title: Noor's Count
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Cross-referencing flicker intervals, Noor calculates the final event: in nineteen days, a gravity pulse large enough to crack the planet's crust unless the creatures receive acknowledgment — or the fleets' weapons do something worse. Emotional beat: a healer forced to deliver a death sentence with a deadline.

chapters.title: What Rhee Kept
chapters.summary: POV: Rhee Voss. At Kestrel, Rhee finds the jamming order bears her dead brother's unit designation — he helped build the blackout. Grief cracks her neutrality; she steals a military cipher key and turns back for Meridian-9. Emotional beat: private loss converted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Third Flicker
chapters.summary: POV: Idris. Two seconds this time. The colony's reactor fails; evacuation ships are forty days out and no longer coming. Idris keeps the wounded alive by hand in the dark, and the survivors begin singing the nine-note motif back at the ice — badly, hopefully. Emotional beat: despair answered by stubborn communion.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Sky
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Concord and Compact advance fleets arrive in orbit ahead of schedule, weapons hot, truce hours from expiry. Both demand the colony's surrender. Jude realizes the only channel neither side will jam is the creatures' own frequency. Emotional beat: the trap closing into a door.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Climax begins: using Rhee's stolen cipher and the ice as an amplifier, Jude transmits the full translation — the peace offer and the proof of the Concord cover-up — on the open tide-frequency, signing it with her own name. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into declaration.

chapters.title: The Answer From Below
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. The creatures respond — a gravity pulse that stops every weapon system in orbit without harming a single ship, then repeats the address slowly, patiently, in every human language they've learned from decades of intercepted traffic. The fleets go silent. Emotional beat: overwhelming awe; being heard at last.

chapters.title: Ceasefire, Extended
chapters.summary: POV: Rhee Voss. Commanders on both sides, confronted with the broadcast and the pulse, extend the truce under mutual suspicion of each other's secrets. Rhee brokers the first joint landing party, lying fluently to both flags to buy the colony time. Emotional beat: weary triumph; peace as improvisation.

chapters.title: Evacuation of the Living
chapters.summary: POV: Noor. Ships arrive — not to erase Meridian-9 but to evacuate it while negotiators descend to the ice. The colonists carry out their dead's names and the archive Idris saved. Jude lingers last, listening to the song continue without needing her. Emotional beat: bittersweet release.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Two Languages
chapters.summary: POV: Jude. Epilogue aboard the negotiation transport: the war is suspended, the inquiry into the cover-up begun, and Jude serves as the first accredited translator between humanity and the tide-minds. That night she dreams in English and tide at once, and both languages say the same word: stay. Emotional beat: belonging, finally earned.
